title: 1961 AHSME Problem 23
statement: Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are both in the line segment \(AB\) and on the same side of its midpoint. \(P\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3,\) and \(Q\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(3:4.\) If \(PQ=2,\) then the length of \(AB\) is:

solutions.text:
The division ratios give \(\frac{AP}{AB}=\frac25\) and \(\frac{AQ}{AB}=\frac37.\) Hence \(PQ=(\frac{3}{7}-\frac{2}{5})AB=\frac{AB}{35}.\) Since \(PQ=2,\) we obtain \(AB=70.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Express \(\frac{AP}{AB}\) and \(\frac{AQ}{AB}\) from the two division ratios
Their difference is the fraction of \(AB\) represented by \(PQ\)
